title: A sandbox without a network boundary is only half a sandbox
summary:
Running untrusted code safely requires more than separating it from the host. You also have to control what that code can reach.

This matters more as AI agents gain the ability to read files, execute commands, install packages, and generate programs of their own. A microVM can prevent that code from accessing the host or another workload. By itself, it cannot stop the code from exfiltrating data, probing internal services, attacking systems elsewhere on the internet, or using credentials available inside the environment.

Isolation without egress control contains the process, not its consequences.

A complete sandbox therefore needs both compute isolation and control over the authority available through its network: where code can connect, which credentials it can use, and how those permissions change throughout the workload’s lifecycle. These controls are part of the security boundary, not protections to bolt on later.

A sandbox has more than one boundary

The universal image switches our default operating system from Amazon Linux to Ubuntu, a lighter and more widely used system across the industry.

title: Introducing Run SDK: secure eval for your agents
summary:
Agents increasingly write TypeScript programs to coordinate tools and process their results. Once those programs touch real applications, some steps require authentication, while others need human approval.

Executing that code with eval gives it the same access as the application around it, including its secrets and internal services, and leaves no durable way to pause at those boundaries.

Today, we're releasing the Run SDK, a package for executing untrusted JavaScript and TypeScript without giving it direct access to your application or system. Applications expose narrow host functions and can interrupt execution for authentication or human-in-the-loop approval. The program resumes after a decision without repeating completed work.

title: The end of credential sprawl for agents
summary:
Every useful agent reaches beyond your codebase. It posts to Slack, opens pull requests, queries Snowflake, or calls an internal API. That reach is what makes it valuable, and it's also where the risk lives, because for years, granting it meant provisioning a long-lived token and hoping it never leaked.

Vercel Connect replaces long-lived tokens with ones your code requests at runtime, scoped to the task and expiring on their own.

During the public beta, we've grown the ecosystem past 100 connectors, unified how they work, and added the governance capabilities teams need in production.

Today, Vercel Connect is generally available.

title: The best workflow engine is a programming language
summary:
The idea of orchestrating long-running, stateful logic on top of unreliable, stateless infrastructure isn't new. We've had message queues, job runners, microservice choreographies, and full-blown workflow engines for a long time. What we never had was a version of it that felt good to write.

I'd spent about six months working on a fork of Temporal, mostly on weekends, trying to turn it into a serverless answer with DX that felt more Vercel-native. Eventually it dawned on me that to ship that experience, I'd need to own the execution environment too. So I dropped the fork, joined Vercel, and started hacking on a new framework from scratch alongside Nathan Rajlich.

title: Scan and search variants with multiple barcodes
summary:
Shopify POS can now identify a product variant using any barcode associated with it, making it easier for staff to find the right product when items have different barcodes across suppliers, channels, or packaging.

What’s new?
Staff can now scan or search for a product variant using any of its associated barcodes, including identifiers such as GTIN, EAN, ASIN, or SKU-based codes. Regardless of which associated barcode is used, Shopify POS will pull up the correct variant.

This reduces the need to manually look up products when the barcode on an item differs from the primary barcode your store typically uses, helping staff find the right item faster during checkout, receiving, and inventory tasks.

This update is automatically available in Shopify POS v11.14. Additional barcodes must first be associated with the product variant in Shopify Admin.

title: Check connectivity status from POS Home
summary:
You can now check your device’s connectivity status directly from POS Home. A new status icon makes it easier for staff to confirm that their device is connected and ready to sell before starting checkout.

What’s new?
Connectivity status has moved from the POS side navigation to POS Home, where it’s visible at a glance. Staff can select the status icon to open a popover with more details about their connection.

By making connectivity easier to find, staff can identify and troubleshoot issues sooner instead of discovering a connection problem in the middle of a sale.

This update is automatically available to all staff on Shopify POS v11.14. No setup or action is required.

title: How we cut CDN metadata lookup latency by 91%
summary:
Every request to Vercel passes through our CDN, which executes on average over 80 million routing instructions per second. Part of that work is looking up metadata to determine which paths exist and how to serve them. When that metadata isn’t cached, the CDN has to fetch it before it can serve the response.

We used to fetch and cache metadata one path at a time, retrieving only what each lookup needed. That seemed efficient at the time, but large deployments can contain hundreds of thousands of paths, each with its own cache entry. Every new deployment introduced fresh metadata, making cache misses a recurring cost for large sites that deployed frequently.

title: TypeSafe AI's Jev now available on AI Gateway
summary:
Jev from TypeSafe AI is now available on AI Gateway.

Jev is a probabilistic decision model for software: state goes in, typed Choice, Score, and Boolean answers come out.

Regular language models generate text one token at a time, which the application then parses and validates. Jev evaluates all declared questions in parallel and returns typed answers plus probabilities directly. That removes unnecessary text generation and makes it straightforward to automate clear cases while routing uncertain ones to review.

TypeSafe reports Jev was up to 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper than LLMs on its workflow evaluations. Example use cases include:

  • Choosing the next tool or subagent in an agent loop

  • Deciding whether to continue, retry, ask the user, or stop

  • Scoring urgency or risk before an action

  • Verifying model outputs and enforcing guardrails.

A Drive is persistent storage that you mount as a directory in a Vercel Sandbox. It isn’t tied to a single sandbox, so you can reuse the same Drive across runs and different sandbox instances.

Use Drives to preserve an agent's workspace or on-disk memory, or to reuse datasets, models, and dependency trees.

Create and mount a Drive

Create or retrieve a Drive and mount it at a path when starting a sandbox. Read and write files through the sandbox filesystem at that path.

Anything stored under /data remains on the Drive after the sandbox stops.

Share Drive data across sandboxes

The new @vercel/connect/tanstack-ai subpath exports connectMCPTransport, which takes a TanStack transport config and attaches a Connect-backed auth provider. The provider is called before every MCP request, so the token is always fresh.

If the user has not granted access, createMCPClient fails with a consent challenge before the model runs. Catch it with getConsentChallenge and redirect to Connect's consent URL. title: Tax is now calculated on return shipping fees
summary:
Starting October 23, 2026, for merchants using Shopify Tax or Tax Platform in the United States, return shipping fees will be taxed like any other shipping charge. Shopify calculates and applies the tax automatically, so you don’t need to fix under-collection on returns.

When you create a return, you’ll see the estimated tax. When you process the return, we record the final amount. These taxes flow into your tax reports automatically.

This update applies to orders shipped to US addresses. Your existing shipping tax settings still apply — if you’ve set shipping to be untaxed in a state, return shipping fees in that state remain untaxed.

*What you need to do: *
- If you use a manual workaround today to calculate, collect, import, or reconcile tax on return shipping fees, review it before October 23 to avoid double-counting tax.
- Otherwise, no action is required.

How it works
* Overrides replace the default return window: If an item matches an override, that override's return window gets applied instead of your default or market-specific window.
* The shortest override wins: If an item matches more than one override, the shortest matching return window applies.
* Final sale still wins: Items marked as final sale can't be returned (or cancelled), even if they also match a return window override.
* Default rules apply otherwise: If an item isn’t final sale and doesn’t match an override, your market-specific return window applies. If no market-specific rules are set, your default return window applies.

title: Vercel Drives is now generally available
summary:
Vercel Drives is now generally available for Vercel Sandbox on Hobby, Pro, and Enterprise.

A Drive is persistent storage that you mount as a directory in a Vercel Sandbox. Its files remain available after the sandbox stops, so later runs and other sandboxes can access them by mounting the same Drive.

Use Drives to preserve an agent’s workspace or file-based memory across runs, or to make datasets, models, dependencies, and build artifacts available across sandboxes.

You can also fork a Drive into independent writable Drives. Forks inherit the source Drive's data, region, and maximum size, then store their own changes. Parallel workers can start with the same files and make changes without affecting the original or one another.

Learn more in the Drives documentation.

title: Death to long-lived static credentials
summary:
Fifteen years ago, TLS was something you'd use to protect the most sensitive areas of your app. Then Google, Let's Encrypt, the EFF, and others led the push for HTTPS everywhere, making encryption the default for every request. Without it, anyone between the browser and server can read and tamper with the traffic.

OAuth, OIDC, DBSC, and related standards already provide building blocks for secure authentication, but standards alone do not make secure methods the norm. HTTPS needed tooling that made encryption easy and a sustained push that made it expected. Machine-to-machine authentication still resembles HTTPS in 2010, with some vendors and enterprises leading the way while long-lived static credentials remain the default for many SaaS vendors and infrastructure providers.

title: Introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway
summary:
Today, we are introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway.

Virtual Models are an abstraction of the model string and configurations your apps and developers use. With a single virtual model ID, you can change and update models, configure fallbacks and priority, and enforce Zero Data Retention centrally. The virtual model configuration applies wherever the ID is used.

Assign a virtual model ID to an agent task, and pass it as the model string wherever that task is called. You can then change the model and settings behind the virtual model ID in AI Gateway, and your apps and agents will pick up the new configuration automatically, without code changes or redeploys.

title: Introducing Vercel CI
summary:
Coding agents are opening more pull requests than ever, and each one waits on CI before anyone can review or merge it. Most CI systems run the entire workflow on every push, even a one-line change. The more your agents push, the more time you spend waiting on CI.

Today, we're announcing Vercel CI in Beta. It runs only the tasks affected by your code change, and spins up only the compute those checks need, the same way Fluid compute scales with your traffic.

At Vercel, our CI now keeps up with our coding agents. Time from git push to "CI passed" is 2-6x faster than it was before.

How it works

Vercel CI uses Turborepo to understand your tasks and which ones depend on each other. It reads turbo.json, so if you're already using Turborepo, there's no separate CI config to write.
